transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-01-12 16:00 PST | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Laura Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE); Maya Thompson (Aurora Head of ML), Ben Cho (Infra Lead), Rita Alvarez (Product), Jordan Price (CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
- Goal: scope a 6-week POC to validate performance and cost for Aurora's chat assistant; identify reserved commit and burst strategy; define benchmarks and pass/fail.
- Key constraints: EU data residency for EU users, private VPC for logs, expected daytime spike to ~12x baseline for 2 hours/day, tail-latency target p95 < 350ms for small prompts, budget guardrails.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, do you all see the agenda? quick intros.
[00:20] Maya: yep, thanks. maya here, i'll give context then hand to ben for infra specifics.
[00:35] Ben: hi, ben, infra lead. our stack is k8s in a private VPC, we run inference behind a gateway, currently using batch gpus on premise but looking to move to hosted or dedicated.
[00:52] Laura: cool, thanks. just to flag, we'll be covering sizing, burst fallback strategies, and a proposed benchmark plan — feel free to interrupt.
[01:12] Jordan: question up front, do you typically recommend full reserved for POC or a hybrid reserved + burst? asking because procurement wants a predictable number.
[01:30] Samir: good question. for POC we usually recommend a modest reserved baseline sized to cover 60-80% of steady throughput, plus burst capacity for peak windows. that keeps predictability while avoiding overcommit.
[01:52] Maya: our steady is small, like 15 requests/sec across EU; spikes go up to 180 rps for 90-120 minutes — it's the morning sync across customers.
[02:12] Laura: got it, that's a 12x spike factor. can you share sequence length distribution? that matters for GPU memory and batch sizing.
[02:28] Maya: yes, i'll share — mostly 32-256 tokens, median 64, 95th at ~220.
[02:40] Diego: ok so peak 180rps at median 64 tokens, what models are you planning to use?
[02:50] Maya: we want an LLM for chat; currently evaluating OpenFamily-13B and AmberLite-7B for latency/cost tradeoffs.
[03:05] Samir: quick note — OpenFamily-13B will need more VRAM and potentially larger instance SKU; AmberLite-7B can fit on smaller GPUs and we can recommend quantization profiles.
[03:22] Ben: another constraint: all EU traffic must stay in eu-west zone and logs must remain in our VPC path. will Redwood's private deployment handle that?
[03:40] Samir: yes, our Private offering supports VPC peering and on-prem connectors; for the POC we can do a Private control plane with customer-managed networking or a dedicated capacity in an EU region. we'll put details in the security pack.
[03:57] Rita: procurement asks: if we reserve, what's our commit term? and is bursting incremental pricing or fixed?
[04:12] Laura: reserved is monthly commit for Dedicated. for POC we often do a short-term reserved with monthly billing pro-rated; burst is metered and we can model cost in the worksheet. we'll show scenarios: 0%, 50%, 100% burst usage during spike windows.
[04:35] Maya: ok sample metrics you need from our side?
[04:42] Samir: traffic logs (rps, payload sizes), sequence-length histogram, SLOs for latency and error rates, spike window times and expected concurrency.
[05:00] Jordan: what's your fallback strategy if reserved capacity is exhausted mid-spike? we cannot have user-facing 5s+ latencies.
[05:12] Laura: we recommend multi-tier fallback: 1) route to a cheaper, smaller model variant with graceful degradation, 2) apply aggressive batching and early-stopping heuristics for non-critical responses, 3) queue with estimated ETA shown to user for long ops, 4) auto-scale additional burst nodes if available. the POC will test routes 1 and 4 in the benchmark.
[05:40] Ben: about the cheaper variant, are there throughput guarantees?
[05:47] Diego: the variant will likely be quantized and lower-parameter; throughput is higher and cost per token lower, but quality may degrade. we'll include a quality delta measurement in the evals.
[06:05] Maya: quality delta is a key success metric. we need rubric: intent preservation 90% of cases and core-slot extraction accuracy > 92% else we fail.
[06:22] Samir: noted. we'll add that to the success criteria doc.

[06:40] Benchmark planning segment:
[06:45] Laura: propose benchmark matrix: steady-state 1-hour run, spike window 2-hour run with controlled ramp to 12x, and long tail 6-hour run to observe degradation. metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, error rate, model output quality by prompt set.
[07:12] Maya: sounds good. can you run the spike window between 08:00-10:00 our local time? that's when our customers autorespond.
[07:22] Samir: yes, we'll schedule benchmarks in that window. we will also provide a runbook for the customer to throttle and capture traces.
[07:36] Ben: on telemetry: we'll need token-level tracing and per-request IDs forwarded to our logging pipeline. is there an integration?
[07:46] Diego: yes we support per-request headers and can forward sampling traces to customer endpoints; for POC we'll enable full traces for the benchmark.
[07:58] Jordan: what about cache/prefix reuse? do you support KV cache across requests to improve latency?
[08:06] Laura: yes, we have KV cache and prefix caching; the POC can test cache warm vs cold to show real-world improvements.

[08:30] Cost modeling conversation:
[08:35] Samir: i'll walk through a quick example scenario on numbers: baseline 10 gpus reserved of mid-range A100 equivalent fits AmberLite-7B with quantization; burst pool of up to 6 additional GPUs for spike. with 2-hour spikes per day your monthly burst cost is X, reserved is Y, combined blended cost per 1k tokens we will show in sheet.
[09:02] Ben: can we set hard budget caps so burst stops if cost > threshold? that's a blocker for procurement.
[09:12] Laura: yes you can set cost-cutoff policies and automated fallback triggers on cost or latency. we'll include policy templates.
[09:22] Rita: how do you handle rollbacks if a new model causes regressions?
[09:27] Diego: Redwood Optimize integrates evals and can auto-fallback to previous model version if quality or latency regress beyond configured thresholds. we'll demo this in the pilot.

[09:45] Technical deep-dive bits (short):
[09:48] Maya: curious about kernel selection and quantization — will you need us to convert model or can you run our own artifacts?
[09:56] Laura: we can stage customer-provided artifacts; for some quantization we use our own compilation step. there may be slight diffs. we'll capture acceptance tests for the fused artifact.
[10:08] Jordan: about data residency, what about logs that include PII? we need KMS/HSM integration for keys.
[10:18] Samir: we support KMS integrations and HSM for private deployments; logs can be forwarded to customer-managed storage inside their VPC.

[10:35] Questions and clarifications:
[10:38] Ben: timeline sanity check — how quickly can you spin up reserved capacity in EU for the POC?
[10:45] Samir: for Dedicated we can provision within 72 hours once purchase order is signed; Private VPC setup takes 5-10 business days depending on networking changes.
[10:58] Maya: procurement review needed — we need a 6-week POC statement of work and SLAs on latency for the period.
[11:08] Samir: we will draft a short SOW with measurable success criteria and include latency SLOs for the POC window.

[11:25] Recap and success criteria (explicit):
[11:30] Laura: Proposed POC success criteria: 1) p95 latency < 350ms for median 64-token prompts under steady load, 2) during spike window 2-hour run, user-facing degradation limited to fallbacks with quality drop <= 10% according to rubric, 3) cost per 1k tokens under agreed budget threshold (to be defined), 4) Private VPC connectivity and log forwarding validated.
[12:02] Maya: agree. add item: automated fallback triggered and rollback policy exercised.
[12:15] Samir: action items and next steps we'll capture in the sheet and follow-up email.

[12:30] Closing notes:
[12:33] Rita: thanks all. please include security docs and billing scenarios in the follow up.
[12:40] Samir: will do. thanks everyone.

References shared in call: Redwood POC capacity worksheet (link in notes), benchmark plan doc (link), SOC2 & Private deployment checklist (link), sample prompt set (attached by Maya in follow-up).

End of transcript.
